<div class="hero"><p class="eyebrow">THE EDGE OF EVIDENCE / LANDSCAPE STUDY 01</p><h1>AI biotech,<br><em>mapped.</em></h1><p class="lede">From biological questions to potential medicines: explore the companies, tools, and therapeutic modalities shaping AI-enabled drug discovery.</p><p class="hero-note">A curated starting set · United States and Europe · Research snapshot: November 11–12, 2026</p><a href="#explore" class="jump">Explore the landscape ↓</a><div class="orb" aria-hidden="true"><span></span><span></span><span></span></div></div>

<section class="intro"><div><p class="eyebrow">HOW TO READ THIS LANDSCAPE</p><h2>Different tools.<br>Different questions.</h2></div><div><p>AI biotech is not one business model or one technology. Some companies develop medicines; others provide tools, data, or partnerships. Many do both. This map follows the work from understanding disease to testing a treatment in people.</p><p>The company set is curated, not a census. A company can appear in more than one stage. Counts describe this dataset only and must not be interpreted as market shares.</p></div></section>

<section class="landscape-brief" aria-labelledby="brief-heading"><div><p class="eyebrow">THE LANDSCAPE / A SHORT READ</p><h2 id="brief-heading">The question is where AI enters the work.</h2></div><div><p>AI biotech spans more than drug design. Some teams use patient and experimental data to identify targets; others design molecules, predict properties, or support clinical trials. The outputs are different: a target hypothesis, a proposed molecule, and a trial prediction each need their own validation.</p><p>Company models differ, too. <a href="https://www.recursion.com/pipeline">Recursion</a> reports an internal therapeutic portfolio alongside partnerships, while <a href="https://boltz.bio/platform">Boltz</a> provides molecular-design tools. The dashboard classifies companies by their reported work; an investment or collaboration alone does not make a partner the owner of a drug.</p><p>Ownership can change along the way. <a href="https://www.pathos.com/pathos-ai-enters-global-licensing-agreement-with-alphamab-oncology-on-jskn016-a-first-in-class-trop2-her3-bispecific-adc">Pathos licenses JSKN016 outside Greater China</a>, while Alphamab retains rights in Greater China. <a href="https://www.flagshippioneering.com/news/press-release/flagship-pioneering-forms-etcelera-to-move-drug-discovery-from-probability-to-prediction">Etcelera</a> combines three discovery platforms, but CLY-124 is being advanced by the separate Cellarity SCD entity. The details matter when comparing pipelines.</p><p>Clinical progress is encouraging, but it does not isolate AI’s contribution to a treatment’s performance. Compare the specific claim with experimental validation, clinical evidence, and the role of the algorithm. Use the profiles below to follow those links.</p></div></section>

<section class="methods"><p class="eyebrow">02 / APPLICATIONS AND METHODS</p><h2>What the models actually do</h2><p>Explore the categories adapted from the supplied drug-discovery framework. Applications, data types and model families are shown separately; a company can appear in several categories. A count of zero means no company is mapped in this preliminary dataset, not that the industry has no such company.</p><div id="application-catalog"></div><p class="taxonomy-note">Framework adapted from Table 3 of <a href="https://www.nature.com/articles/s41573-026-01496-2">Bender et al., “Artificial intelligence in drug discovery — what it is, where we stand and the path forward,” <em>Nature Reviews Drug Discovery</em> (2026) ↗</a>. Categories and descriptions are paraphrased and reorganized. Target identification, virtual screening, oligonucleotide design, drug repurposing and physics-based simulation were added to reflect this landscape’s scope. Company classifications link to supporting sources in each profile.</p></section>

<section class="repurposing"><p class="eyebrow">A DIFFERENT ROUTE / REPURPOSING</p><h2>A new use for an existing medicine</h2><p>Repurposing starts with a molecule that already exists and asks whether it might work in another disease. The approach can combine literature mining, knowledge graphs, biological data and experiments; it is a development strategy, not a therapeutic modality.</p><p>Baricitinib illustrates both the opportunity and the need for evidence. BenevolentAI reported identifying the existing drug as a candidate for COVID-19. The FDA subsequently approved it for a defined hospitalized adult population in 2022. This was a new indication for an existing medicine; clinical testing and regulatory review supported the approval. <a href="https://www.benevolent.com/news-and-media/press-releases-and-in-media/benevolentai-appoints-daniel-neil-chief-technology-officer/">Company disclosure ↗</a> · <a href="https://www.fda.gov/drugs/novel-drug-approvals-fda/new-drug-therapy-approvals-2022">FDA approval summary ↗</a></p></section>

<section class="evidence"><div><p class="eyebrow">03 / READING THE EVIDENCE</p><h2>A pipeline is not proof<br>of an algorithm.</h2></div><div><p>A predicted structure, a laboratory hit, and a clinical result answer different questions. A candidate reaching a clinical trial shows development progress; it does not, by itself, prove that AI improved clinical outcomes or was responsible for every step of its discovery.</p><p>Company descriptions and pipeline stages below are linked to their sources. Partnered and owned programs are distinguished where disclosed. Missing information is labeled as such.</p></div></section>

<section class="methodology"><p class="eyebrow">ABOUT THIS DATA</p><h2>Scope &amp; limitations</h2><p>This exploratory dataset includes selected AI-native therapeutic developers and specialist computational providers headquartered in the US or Europe. Schrödinger is included as a specialist provider with a longer history in physics-based computation. It excludes large pharma, manufacturing-only tools, and general-purpose technology vendors. Inclusion depends on public source material and is not exhaustive. Categories are editorial classifications and multiple labels may apply. Oligonucleotides are a distinct modality. Asset stages can change; check the linked source before making a decision.</p><p>Platform descriptions are primarily company-reported. Public/private listing status does not establish a controlling shareholder; company profiles identify undisclosed control and contractual rights. Company portfolio summaries describe disclosed programs and cannot enumerate confidential assets. Registry records include historical and terminated studies; sponsorship is not equivalent to asset ownership.</p><p>Research snapshot: November 11–12, 2026. Public information cannot establish a perfect census of private companies or disclose every cap table and contract. This project uses a documented, repeatable review of identified records and marks unverified details. <a href="company-audit.csv">Download the company and rights audit ↗</a> · <a href="ownership-audit.csv">Download dated investor and ownership evidence ↗</a> · <a href="asset-audit.csv">Download selected asset-level evidence ↗</a> · <a href="pipeline-coverage.csv">Download the company-by-company pipeline review ↗</a> · <a href="trial-audit.csv">Download the selected ClinicalTrials.gov audit ↗</a> · <a href="sponsor-search-audit.csv">Download the sponsor-search log ↗</a>. Sponsor searches cover all companies using a specified name or alias; they are not a comprehensive listing of all aliases, partner studies or global trials.</p><p>Design and content prepared with AI assistance; author review is required before publication.</p></section>
